newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent falls on NYMEX losses, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent falls on NYMEX losses, profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent futures pared earlier gains as the market tracked the volatile action on NYMEX where the May crude oil contract closes at the end of the session, traders said.
IPE June Brent was trading 16 cents lower $18.18 a barrel at 1456 GMT, having traded as high as $18.64 earlier on.
"We thought this afternoon might be a bit rocky," said one trader. "The market's basically being pulled about by action on NYMEX."
The NYMEX May contract was trading 57 cents a barrels lower at $19.81 a barrel.
Traders also attributed some of the losses to profit-taking.
"I don't think the market was entirely comfortable at the higher levels," one trader said.
Traders said IPE Brent had been helped higher earlier by news that crude oil exports out of Nigeria were subject to delay due to a strike by contractors at the tanker terminal.
The strike had forced Shell to declare a force majeure on Bonny crude oil, which accounts for about half its 950,000 barrels per day (bpd) Nigerian output, with effect from Monday.
